prior_description: long_names.py removes the global floor by allowing negative free names and taking a fresh negative integer larger in magnitude than a decimal encoding of the present sequent.
prior_status: Not a certified kernel: no complete alias audit or new producer; rapidly growing names; 566 bytes / 272 tokens / 317 AST nodes reported.
search_scope: All integrated .py/.py.gz, article and README/proof-note text; all four current incoming packages extracted and text-searched.
safe_novelty_claim: A completed soundness/completeness audit and smaller implementation of an existing unselected decimal-name idea, if actually established. Do not claim invention of magnitude-based scalar freshness.
freshness_lemma: For a finite tree X of exact integers and lists, each integer leaf v has at most len(str(X)) decimal digits; therefore abs(v)<10**len(str(X)), and p=-10**len(str(X)) is not an old name. Set X=[g,a,r] to cover context, goal and every packet field.
conditions: All names are exact integer leaves; floating exponent spelling does not support the magnitude argument.
Every raw metadata field later used for the rule must be covered before allocating p.
Operations used before opening must introduce no new numerical names outside the covered support; padding-depth arithmetic deserves explicit audit.
Contexts are persistent copies, not in-place shared mutations.
Future input may legitimately refer to p inside its scope; freshness is local to the rule, not global freshness against the entire remaining stream.
resources: Repeated naming can grow decimal widths exponentially or worse along branches.
CPython decimal integer conversion has a default digit limit, commonly 4300; generated names can hit it even if initial input integers are short.

A claim of canonical completeness must idealize unbounded integer-to-string conversion or include/document removal of this runtime limit; finite practical examples should report the actual configuration.
expression_notes: Base 10 is the smallest positive integer base whose power at a decimal-length bound gives the simple universal magnitude domination argument. Replacing 10 by 9 or 2 is not justified.
The outer structured list [g,a,r] avoids type requirements on a; g+a+r is shorter only if all three are lists at every evaluated naming site.
~10**N is also negative and fresh, equal to -(10**N)-1, without outer parentheses. It is a spelling refinement, not a new principle.
